fixes.explanation: Judges is a fair guess after all that fire, baker. But Moses turns to the LORD and says, "Surely You love the people…" (Deuteronomy 33:3). Flaming fire and myriads of holy ones in verse 2, and I'd be hiding behind my oven. Moses walks right up and talks about love.

Law is it, friend. Moses says each one receives His words, "…the law that Moses gave us, the possession of the assembly of Jacob." (Deuteronomy 33:4). A possession is something you hold on to. I think Moses is saying the whole assembly of Jacob owns this law, like a family guarding the one cookie recipe nobody is allowed to lose.

False is right, baker. Moses says, "Let Reuben live and not die, nor his men be few." (Deuteronomy 33:6). He's asking that Reuben's men not be few. One verse for Reuben, and it's all about staying alive and staying counted.

Bethel and Shiloh are good guesses, baker, but Moses doesn't name them here. In verse 8 he says the LORD tested Levi at Massah and contested him "…at the waters of Meribah." Those are his two places. Listen for the waters and you land on Meribah.

Gilgal and Ai aren't in this blessing, friend. Moses says the LORD tested Levi at Massah and contested him "…at the waters of Meribah." (Deuteronomy 33:8). Meribah is the one that comes with the waters. Next time, let the word waters walk you to Meribah.

Land isn't the reason Moses gives, friend. He says Levi disregarded his brothers and didn't know his own sons "…for he kept Your word and maintained Your covenant." (Deuteronomy 33:9). I think that's a heavy thing to read about a man's own family. The reason Moses names is Levi's hold on God's word and covenant.

This one is true, baker. Moses says of Levi, "He will teach Your ordinances to Jacob and Your law to Israel…" (Deuteronomy 33:10). Imagine being handed a whole nation as your class. I can barely keep one batch of dough in line.

Elders at the gate don't show up in Joseph's blessing, baker. Moses names "…the favor of Him who dwelt in the burning bush." Then he asks, "May these rest on the head of Joseph and crown the brow of the prince of his brothers." (Deuteronomy 33:16). That's the favor he asks for, and it's the LORD's.

Perez and Zerah are sons of Judah (Genesis 46:12), so they come from a different family line. Joseph's blessing closes with "Such are the myriads of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh." (Deuteronomy 33:17). Those are Joseph's two sons (Genesis 41:51-52). Easy to mix up when everybody's related.

Gershon and Kohath are sons of Levi (Genesis 46:11), so they belong back with Levi's blessing. Joseph's blessing closes with "Such are the myriads of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh." (Deuteronomy 33:17). Those are Joseph's two sons (Genesis 41:51-52). Right family, different brother, friend.

Sacrifices of righteousness, friend. Moses says of Zebulun and Issachar, "They will call the peoples to a mountain; there they will offer sacrifices of righteousness." (Deuteronomy 33:19). One tribe is told to rejoice in journeys and the other in tents. Both end up calling the peoples to the same mountain.

A bear would be a mighty pick, but Moses doesn't use it. He says Gad "lies down like a lion…" (Deuteronomy 33:20). Gad is compared to a lion, not called one. And a lion's cub comes up again in Dan's blessing.

A census is a fair guess, baker, but it's not in this verse. Moses says Gad "…administered the LORD’s justice and His ordinances for Israel." (Deuteronomy 33:21). The justice and ordinances belong to the LORD, and Gad carried them out for the whole nation. I can barely administer who gets the last cookie on the plate.

Moses doesn't mention the tabernacle in Gad's blessing, baker. He says Gad chose the best land, came with the leaders of the people, and "…administered the LORD’s justice and His ordinances for Israel." (Deuteronomy 33:21). Those are the things the verse names for Gad. Building isn't on the list.

Gilead is a good guess, friend, but Moses doesn't use it here. He says, "Dan is a lion’s cub, leaping out of Bashan." (Deuteronomy 33:22). Bashan is the place he names. Everything else in Dan's blessing is that one leaping cub.

Darkness feels like something God would chase off, friend, but Moses names something else. He says, "He drives out the enemy before you…" (Deuteronomy 33:27). I spent years in a dark junk drawer, so I'd cheer for that too. But in this verse the enemy is what gets driven out.
Securely, friend. Moses says, "So Israel dwells securely…" (Deuteronomy 33:28). The land has grain and new wine, and even the heavens drip with dew. I think that's a pretty peaceful picture of home.

Briefly is about how long, baker, but Moses is talking about how Israel lives. He says, "So Israel dwells securely; the fountain of Jacob lives untroubled…" (Deuteronomy 33:28). I'd take untroubled over a day off any time.

A people saved by the LORD, baker. Moses asks, "Blessed are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD?" (Deuteronomy 33:29). Saved is the word he puts on Israel. Then he keeps going and calls the LORD their shield and sword.

This one is true, baker. Moses says of the LORD, "He is the shield that protects you, the sword in which you boast." (Deuteronomy 33:29). Look at what Israel boasts in. I think it's pretty great that the sword they brag about is the LORD Himself.
